title: Static export and precomputed interaction
summary: Shipping a site as plain files with no server, and making it interactive by committing captured state instead of querying a backend.
what: Every route is rendered to HTML at build time. There is no server process, no API and no database behind the site.
why: Hosting is free and the attack surface is essentially zero. The constraint is that nothing can run a live query.
how: Interactive elements replay real state captured offline: run the pipeline, capture the intermediate results, commit them as JSON, and let the client move between them.
in_this_project: The site renders committed JSON and never queries the platform. Interactive demos read from data/interactive/, where each dataset carries the script that produced it and the command that regenerates it. The demos degrade honestly: with JavaScript disabled the reader still gets the full table of figures rendered server-side, not a blank box.

advantages: Free hosting, no runtime to attack
Content is present without JavaScript and is indexable
Every figure traces to a committed file
limitations: Demo data must be regenerated when the pipeline changes

pitfalls: Synthesising demo data because the real pipeline is not ready
Interactive states with no number attached

use: Documentation and result sites whose data changes on a build cadence
